title: How Long Does Carpet Installation Take? A Room-by-Room Timeline
meta: One bedroom takes about an hour, a staircase half a day, a whole Everett house one or two days. Wills Flooring lays out the carpet install timeline by room.
keywords: how long does carpet installation take, carpet installation time per room, how long to carpet a whole house, carpet installation Everett WA, carpet install timeline stairs

blocks.lead: A single bedroom takes about an hour to carpet, a staircase two to four hours, and a typical three-bedroom Everett house is done in one long day or two comfortable ones.
blocks.detail: Tear-out, furniture, seams and stairs are what stretch a job. Add one to two weeks before install day for the carpet to arrive after you choose it at the free in-home estimate, and you have the whole timeline.

blocks.html: Everett homeowners ask this for practical reasons: a Boeing shift schedule to work around, a tenant moving into a Silver Lake rental on the first, or a Port Gardner condo with a four-hour elevator reservation. So instead of a vague "it depends," here is what each room actually takes, what makes a job run long, and how the days line up from the estimate to the last vacuum pass.

blocks.text: Room-by-room: how long each space takes

head: Space
Install time
What changes it
rows: A closet adds 15 minutes. Furniture left in the room adds 20 to 30 minutes for moving and working around it.
Two doorways and a closet with shelving means more cuts and often a seam at the closet door.
Every doorway is a cut and a transition. A 1990s Eastmont two-story with five bedroom doors off one hall takes the full hour.
Rooms wider than 12 ft need a seam. Seaming, pattern matching and stretching in two directions add the time.
Pie-shaped winders, open sides and a landing push this toward four hours.
Basement or bonus room, 400 sq ft
Concrete slabs need a different tack strip and often a moisture check first; posts and bulkheads add cuts.
Whole 1,600 sq ft house, 3 bedrooms, hall, living room, stairs
Tear-out of the old carpet, four or more seams and stairs make this a two-day job for one crew.
blocks.note: Times are for a two-person Wills Flooring crew on stretch-in carpet over pad. Glue-down and commercial installs run differently.

blocks.text: What a typical Everett install day looks like

items.text: Old carpet is cut into strips, rolled, and carried out with the pad. Tack strip is inspected and replaced where rusty or loose. Staples come out of stairs one by one.
items.note: About 20 minutes per room, an hour for stairs.

items.text: Squeaks get screwed down, high nails set, and any soft spot gets flagged. In Riverside and Bayside homes from the 1910s and 20s this is where we find uneven planks that need a skim of patch before pad goes down.
New pad rolled out, seams taped, stapled every few inches. Tack strip nailed around the room perimeter about a half inch off the wall.
Carpet is rough-cut in the largest room, seams ironed with hot-melt tape, then power-stretched wall to wall and hooked on the tack strip. Trimmed and tucked at the base.
Stairs last, since they are the slowest. Doorway transitions to hardwood, tile or vinyl plank are set and the seams to the hall are finished.
Every room is vacuumed, scraps are hauled off, and you walk it with the crew lead. You can put furniture back immediately.
items.note: No cure time with stretch-in carpet.

blocks.text: What makes a carpet job run long

items.title: Furniture still in the rooms
items.text: A cleared room is an hour. The same room with a bed, dresser and a desk full of cables is closer to two, because the crew moves everything twice and works in halves. We move furniture when asked, but clearing it yourself is the fastest thing you can do for the schedule.

items.title: Tear-out and disposal
items.text: Pulling old carpet, pad and thousands of staples adds a quarter to a third to the day. Old glued-down pad on a slab, common in Everett daylight basements, can add hours of scraping before new pad goes down, and disposal means a second trip to the truck for every room.

items.title: Seams and patterns
items.text: Any room wider than 12 ft gets a seam, since carpet comes in 12 ft rolls. Patterned or striped carpet has to be matched at every seam and on every stair tread, which can double the cutting time on a hallway and stair run.

items.title: Old houses and odd rooms
items.text: Riverside bungalows with out-of-square rooms, bay windows and radiators need many more cuts than a 2005 Silver Lake box. Closets under stairs, angled walls in attic bedrooms and built-in cabinets are the slowest square footage in the house by far.

items.title: Condo logistics
items.text: Port Gardner and downtown Everett buildings often require an elevator reservation, a loading zone and work only between 9 and 5. A job that is four hours of actual work can occupy a full day on the calendar once the building rules are added.

items.title: Subfloor surprises
items.text: A soft spot near a slider, a damp basement slab or a squeak that turns out to be a cracked joist stops the clock until it is fixed. We check the subfloor at the estimate to catch most of this ahead of install day.

blocks.title: Everett rental turnover tip:
blocks.text: If a tenant leaves on the 30th and the next one arrives on the 1st, book the estimate two to three weeks before move-out so the carpet is in our warehouse on the 30th. Tear-out and install on a vacant 1,000 sq ft unit is one day. The bottleneck is never the install; it is choosing the carpet late.

blocks.text: How to keep your install to one day

items.html: Clear everything, including closet floors. Small items in boxes, electronics unplugged, beds broken down. Our carpet prep checklist covers the details.
Choose the carpet early. Material lead time is the longest part of the process. Picking at the estimate instead of a week later saves a week.
Pick an in-stock line if the date is fixed. We bring both in-stock and special-order samples and tell you which is which.
Decide about the stairs up front. Adding stairs on install day means a second trip. Deciding at the estimate keeps it one visit.

Ask for the arrival window and the crew size in writing. Wills Flooring's carpet installation quote lists both, along with tear-out and furniture moving if you want them, with a 1-year workmanship warranty.

faq.q: How long does it take to install carpet in one room?
faq.a: An empty 12 by 12 bedroom takes 45 to 75 minutes including pad and tack strip. Add 15 minutes for a closet, 20 to 30 if furniture stays in the room, and 20 minutes to tear out old carpet. A crew usually schedules a single room as a half-day visit with travel and setup.

faq.q: How long does it take to carpet a whole house?
faq.a: A typical three-bedroom Everett house with a hall, living room and one staircase takes one long day or two comfortable days for a two-person crew, including tear-out. Larger homes with several seams, two staircases or basements run two to three days. Rooms are usable as each one is finished.

faq.q: Can you walk on new carpet right away?
faq.a: Yes. Stretch-in carpet over pad has no glue to cure, so you can walk on it and move furniture back as soon as the crew finishes vacuuming. Glue-down carpet, used mostly in commercial spaces, needs to stay clear for about 24 hours.

faq.q: How far in advance should I schedule carpet installation in Everett?
faq.a: Two to three weeks is comfortable. The estimate takes an hour, in-stock carpet arrives in a few days and special orders take one to three weeks. Install dates are usually available within a week of the material landing. For a rental turnover, book the estimate before the tenant moves out.

faq.q: Do I need to remove old carpet before installation?
faq.a: No. Tear-out and disposal of old carpet and pad are part of the job when you ask for them, and it adds roughly a quarter to a third to the install time. If you want to pull it yourself to save money, leave the tack strip in place unless it is rusty or damaged.

faq.q: Does carpet installation take longer in a condo?
faq.a: The work itself takes the same time, but the day is longer. Buildings like those near Port Gardner require elevator reservations, loading zone timing and quiet hours, so a four-hour job often occupies a full calendar day. We coordinate with the building manager before install day.
